correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact identification of common-knowledge accessibility with the join; proved singleton probability and Bonferroni correction, then bounded all nonsingleton cut events uniformly. Small cuts have geometric majorant O(epsilon_n^2)=o(lambda_n); large cuts have binomial entropy H_(n,k) with exponent -(r-1+o(1))H_(n,k), so their sum is superpolynomially small. For fixed r>=2, lambda_n=n(B_(n-1)/B_n)^r tends to zero; two common singleton intersections are o(lambda_n). A published Bell-ratio asymptotic converts the leading equivalent to (log n)^r/n^(r-1). Direct finite enumeration and exact connected recurrences agree for n<=5 and r=2,3. Unproved limit cases (r growing, nonuniform frames) are excluded.

originality.rationale: Pittel 2000, Theorem 5 is the same random partition-join problem, but gives only an O((log n)^(r+1)/n^(r-1)) upper bound and the probability-one limit. Here the sharp equivalent is n(B_(n-1)/B_n)^r, with conditional uniqueness of a globally singleton world. Pittel neither states nor implies this leading constant from his upper bound alone. Zenger supplies S5 common-knowledge semantics but no random-frame asymptotic; Bell et al supply general component principles but no this rate. Searches of records and primary text did not reveal exact or stronger coverage. A more general uninspected result could still subsume the rate.
residual_risks: Classical general transfer theorems for logarithmic combinatorial classes may subsume the rare-singleton asymptotic; the inspected Bender et al text did not resolve this completely.

value.rationale: Random finite equivalence frames are a canonical S5/common-knowledge model, and Pittel’s same-object theorem leaves a logarithmic gap in the quantitative disconnection probability. The sharp missing log and one-singleton conditional shape describe the dominant rare failure mechanism and can guide finite random epistemic-model construction. The advance is a motivated sharp rate and structural law, not a routine table recalculation or an arbitrary parameter slice.
